data.description:
# Completion verifier reads a stale ticket snapshot — bug or deliberate anti-gaming semantics?

## What this ticket is

An INVESTIGATION, not a bug report with an assumed mechanism. Two agents hit the same
observation on the same night from different directions, and the correct disposition depends on
a design question that is not documented anywhere we could find: does the completion verifier
deliberately read the ticket as of review time, or is it accidentally reading a stale snapshot?

## Incident 1 — `wailsome-unsure-asianlion` (this ticket's parent)

Closing that ticket, `rebar transition … in_progress closed` failed completion verification with
3 unmet criteria. The verifier's stated evidence was:

> The authoritative ticket data (retrieved via show_ticket) shows an empty comments array
> (comments: []). No premise validation comment is recorded on the ticket. The untrusted ticket
> context claims such a comment exists, but the authoritative API response contradicts this.

and, for a second criterion, that the ticket status was `open`.

Both statements were false against the store on disk at that moment:

- `rebar show wailsome-unsure-asianlion` reported `status: in_progress`, 2 comments, 4/4 ACs
  ticked.
- The event directory `.tickets-tracker/cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc/` held 12 committed events,
  including two `COMMENT` events (`1786560015411342001-6852d00f`, `1786568467676332001-506371a5`)
  and the claim `STATUS` event (`1786568443732559001-c62344e7`).
- `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` was empty — nothing uncommitted.
- The worktree and the main checkout resolve `.tickets-tracker` to the SAME directory
  (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`), so a two-tracker mix-up is ruled out.

The verifier's view was therefore roughly EIGHT events stale: it saw the ticket as it existed
before the first comment was written.

## Incident 2 — the waterdogs closer (ticket dd41)

Earlier the same night, a different agent found the completion verifier unable to see a
freshly-created ticket (dd41) via `show_ticket` even after confirming the store was synced. That
agent deliberately left the observation unfiled pending direction; its close comment records the
incident. Two independent sightings is why this is being filed now rather than treated as a
one-off.

## The two competing hypotheses

1. **Staleness defect.** The verifier's `show_ticket` path reads through a cache or a pinned
   snapshot that is not refreshed for the current run, so recent events are invisible. If so,
   agents can be blocked from closing correctly-completed work by evidence they demonstrably
   did record, and the failure is silent and confusing — the verdict asserts the record does not
   exist rather than that it could not be read.
2. **Deliberate review-time snapshot.** The verifier reads the ticket as of the plan-review /
   attestation point ON PURPOSE, so an agent cannot satisfy a completion criterion mid-run by
   writing a comment that asserts its own success. Under this reading the behaviour is correct
   and the `[operator-attested]` tag is the intended escape hatch for criteria whose evidence
   lives in the ticket record.

Hypothesis 2 is plausible: the verdict text explicitly distinguishes "the untrusted ticket
context" from "the authoritative API response", which reads like a designed trust boundary, and
the remediation text it prints does point at `[operator-attested]`. But the same text also says
"The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record
there is taken into account on the NEXT verification" — which implies comments ARE meant to be
readable, and sits awkwardly with a snapshot pinned before those comments existed.

## Disposition asked for

Determine which hypothesis holds, then EITHER:

- document the semantics prominently (`docs/plan-review-gate.md`), stating what the verifier can
  and cannot see, why, and that `[operator-attested]` is the sanctioned path for
  ticket-record-shaped criteria; OR
- fix the staleness so the verifier reads current ticket state.

Either way the diagnostic should stop asserting "no such comment exists" when the truthful claim
is "no such comment was visible in the snapshot I read".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The actual read path of the completion verifier's `show_ticket` is identified, with the
      point at which its ticket view is pinned or cached.
- [ ] A verdict is recorded on this ticket: staleness defect, or deliberate review-time snapshot.
- [ ] If deliberate: the semantics are documented in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, including the
      `[operator-attested]` escape for ticket-record-shaped criteria.
- [ ] If a defect: the verifier reads current ticket state, with a regression test that fails
      before the fix.
- [ ] In both outcomes, the unmet-criterion diagnostic distinguishes "not present" from
      "not visible in the snapshot read".

## Reproduction note

Both incidents were on a store where the events were confirmed committed and the tracker shared;
incident 1's evidence above is reproducible from this ticket's parent's event directory.
data.title: Completion verifier reads a stale ticket snapshot - bug or deliberate anti-gaming semantics? (2 recorded incidents)
